METHODOLOGY_2_Hamiltonian_Energy_Convent: A frequent source of numerical discrepancy across Ising and QUBO software libraries is the factor of $0.5$ on pairwise coupling terms. `thermo-physics` strictly adheres to the standard statistical physics undirected convention. ### A. The Standard Undirected Ising Hamiltonian For an undirected graph $G = (V, E)$ represented by a symmetric coupling matrix $J \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times N}$ ($J_{ij} = J_{ji}$ with zero diagonal $J_{ii} = 0$) and external magnetic field vector $h \in \mathbb{R}^N$: $$E(s) = -\frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^N J_{ij} s_i s_j - \sum_{i=1}^N h_i s_i + E_{\text{offset}} = -\frac{1}{2} s^T J s - h^T s + E_{\text{offset}}$$ where spins $s_i \in \{-1, +1\}$. > [!IMPORTANT] > **The 0.5 Pre-Factor Rule:** > When the double sum $\sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^N J_{ij} s_i s_j$ is evaluated over a full symmetric matrix, every physical undirected edge $\{i, j\}$ is counted twice ($J_{ij} s_i s_j + J_{ji} s_j s_i$). The factor $\frac{1}{2}$ cancels this double counting: > $$
METHODOLOGY_3_Ground-Truth_Exact_Verific: For system sizes up to $N = 24$, the total state space is: $$|\Omega| = 2^{24} = 16,777,216 \text{ configurations}$$ ### A. Exhaustive Vectorized Enumeration Using bit-shift matrix indexing, all $2^{24}$ states are enumerated in vectorized 32-bit chunks: $$E_0 = \min_{s \in \{-1, +1\}^N} \left(-\frac{1}{2} s^T J s - h^T s\right)$$ For Station 10 (Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with quenched Gaussian seed 42): $$E_0 = -15.42659072466675 \quad (E_0 / N = -0.6428)$$ ### B. Single-Spin Flip Stability Criterion Any candidate global minimum $s^*$ must satisfy strict local stability across all $N$ single-spin coordinate directions: $$\Delta E_i = E(s^{* \oplus i}) - E(s^*) = 2 s_i^* \left(\sum_{j=1}^N J_{ij} s_j^* + h_i\right) \ge 0 \quad \forall i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$$ ---
METHODOLOGY_4_MCMC_Mixing_Diagnostics_So: Raw hardware clock rate (sample sweeps per second, Hz) is **not** an accurate measure of computational throughput on frustrated energy landscapes. Highly correlated samples provide diminishing statistical information. ### A. Normalized Autocorrelation via FFT For a scalar observable sequence $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^N$ (e.g. instantaneous Hamiltonian energy $E_t$ or magnetization $M_t$), let $\bar{X} = \frac{1}{N} \sum X_t$. The sample autocorrelation at lag $k$ is: $$\hat{\rho}(k) = \frac{\frac{1}{N-k} \sum_{t=1}^{N-k} (X_t - \bar{X})(X_{t+k} - \bar{X})}{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{t=1}^N (X_t - \bar{X})^2}$$ This is evaluated in $\mathcal{O}(N \log N)$ operations using zero-padded Fast Fourier Transforms: $$\hat{C} = \operatorname{IFFT}\left(|\operatorname{FFT}(X - \bar{X})|^2\right)$$ ### B. Sokal's Self-Consistent Truncation Window The integrated autocorrelation time is defined as: $$\tau_{\text{int}} = \frac{1}{2} + \sum_{k=1}^\infty \rho(k)$$ Summing over all lags $k \to N$ introduces high variance
METHODOLOGY_5_Total_Variation_TV_Distanc: For small solvable graphs ($N \le 8$), we verify that empirical frequencies converge to the exact Boltzmann-Gibbs distribution: $$P_{\text{Boltzmann}}(s) = \frac{e^{-\beta E(s)}}{Z(\beta)}, \quad Z(\beta) = \sum_{s \in \{-1, +1\}^N} e^{-\beta E(s)}$$ The Total Variation distance is: $$D_{\text{TV}}(P_{\text{empirical}}, P_{\text{Boltzmann}}) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{s \in \Omega} |P_{\text{empirical}}(s) - P_{\text{Boltzmann}}(s)|$$ A sampling run is certified as Boltzmann equilibrium if: $$D_{\text{TV}} \le 0.05 \quad (\text{with } N_{\text{samples}} \ge 10,000)$$ ---
